info.title: VeriWorkly API
info.description:
The official API reference for VeriWorkly.

### Authentication Methods

VeriWorkly supports two authentication methods:

#### 1. API Key Authentication (recommended for scripts and integrations)
For programmatic access, send your key either way — both are accepted:

- `X-API-Key: vw_...`
- `Authorization: Bearer vw_...`

A key is **required** for any request that does not originate from a whitelisted VeriWorkly
origin, including requests made from these documentation pages.

- **Format**: `vw_` followed by 64 hexadecimal characters.
- **Rate limit**: 20 requests per 15 minutes per key by default, configurable per key at
  creation up to 600 (the server's `API_KEY_MAX_RATE_LIMIT`). Responses carry
  `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`.
- **Scopes**: keys are scope-gated. A key missing a route's required scope gets `403`. Session
  callers are never scope-gated.

#### 2. Session Authentication (dashboard only)
Used internally by the VeriWorkly dashboard and resume builder, via secure HTTP-only cookies
issued by Better Auth.

- **Cookies**:
  - Local: `veriworkly-auth.session_token`
  - Production: `__Secure-veriworkly-auth.session_token`
- **Note**: sessions are only honoured for whitelisted origins. Send `credentials: 'include'`
  (fetch) or `withCredentials: true` (axios). Requests from these documentation pages **must**
  use an API key.
- **Cookie domain**: when the server sets `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`, the session cookie is issued
  for that domain so it is shared across its subdomains. Without it the cookie belongs to the
  API host only.

#### Endpoints that need neither
These are fully open, with no key, session or first-party origin:

- `GET /api/v1/health` and `GET /api/v1/health/ready`
- `POST /api/v1/affiliates/click` and `GET /api/v1/affiliates/leaderboard` (while the
  affiliate program is switched on)
- the Better Auth routes under `/api/v1/auth/*`
- `POST /api/v1/contact`

Everything else, including the endpoints labelled "public" such as public portfolios and
share links, requires an API key or a whitelisted first-party origin, and returns `401`
without one.

#### Cross-origin requests
A browser request whose `Origin` is not on the server's allowlist is refused with `403`,
message "Not allowed by CORS" and `details.code` `CORS_REJECTED`, whatever credentials it
carries. Requests without an `Origin` header (scripts, servers) are not affected.

### Response Envelope

Every endpoint under `/api/v1` except the Better Auth routes at `/api/v1/auth/*` returns
`{ success, message, data }` on success and `{ success, message, statusCode, details? }` on
failure. Better Auth endpoints return their own payload shapes. `details` is an array of
`{ path, message }` on a validation failure and an object (such as `{ code }`) elsewhere.

A body larger than the route accepts is refused with `413` "Request body too large". Most
routes accept 100 kb; documents, the master profile, profile imports, share links and the
portfolio draft accept 4 MB; the AI and ATS text routes accept 256 kb. A body that is not
valid JSON is refused with `400` "Invalid JSON body".

### Sign-in coverage
Better Auth answers every path under `/api/v1/auth/*`. This reference documents the email
code sign-in (`/email-otp/send-verification-otp`, `/sign-in/email-otp`),
`/get-session` and `/sign-out`, which are the supported way to sign in from your own
client. Better Auth's other routes are also served: social sign-in and account linking (Google, GitHub
and LinkedIn when configured, through `/sign-in/social`, `/link-social` and `/callback/{provider}`),
session management (`/list-sessions`, `/revoke-session`, `/revoke-sessions`,
`/revoke-other-sessions`) and `/email-otp/request-password-reset`. Those follow Better
Auth's own documentation and are not described here. `/forget-password/email-otp` is
switched off. A linked GitHub account cannot be removed (`/unlink-account` answers `403`
with code `GITHUB_UNLINK_FORBIDDEN`), and an account can link only one GitHub account
(`GITHUB_ALREADY_LINKED`, sent as an `error` query parameter on the OAuth redirect, or as a
`403` code elsewhere).

### Not Documented Here

`POST /api/v1/client-errors` (crash reports from VeriWorkly's own site),
`GET /api/v1/health/metrics` and `GET /api/v1/health/jobs` (behind the server's internal key)
and everything under `/api/v1/admin/*` are internal first-party routes. They are left out
of this reference on purpose and are not part of the supported public API.

### Contact form
`POST /api/v1/contact` sends a message to the VeriWorkly team. It is open (no key or
session) and limited to 5 requests per hour per IP. The JSON body takes `name` (1 to 100
characters), `email` (up to 254), `subject` (1 to 200), `message` (10 to 5,000) and `_ts`,
the time the form was loaded in milliseconds since the epoch, which is required. `website`
is a hidden field that must stay empty. A bad body answers `400` "Validation failed" with
`details`; success answers `{ name, email, subject, timestamp }` with the message "Message
sent successfully". A submission sent less than 1.2 seconds after `_ts`, or with `website`
filled, gets the same success answer and is dropped.

get.description:
Lightweight liveness probe. Confirms the API process is up and responding.

It deliberately touches **no** external dependency — no database query, no Redis command — so
that frequent uptime polling does not keep database compute awake. It therefore cannot report
on PostgreSQL or Redis, and never returns `503`. For dependency health use
`GET /api/v1/health/ready`.

It requires no session, no API key and no first-party origin, and it is not rate limited.
The other fully open endpoints are listed in the introduction.

Deep readiness probe for deploy gates and manual diagnostics. Runs a `SELECT 1` against
PostgreSQL and a `PING` against Redis, and returns `503` if either is unreachable.

Because it wakes database compute on every call, prefer `GET /api/v1/health` for routine
uptime monitoring. Like the liveness probe, it requires no authentication.

200.description: Database and Redis are both reachable

503.description:
The database or Redis could not be reached. `details` gives the state of each:
`connected`, `timeout` or `error`. The underlying error is logged server-side only.

get.description:
Retrieves account metadata for the currently authenticated user. Requires the `user:read`
scope when called with an API key.

This returns identity metadata only — resume, cover letter, and portfolio content is never
exposed here. Results are cached for 30 minutes and refreshed on write.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes the authenticated user's account with its documents, portfolio, share
links, API keys and profile, then clears the session cookies. This cannot be undone.

Billing and payout records are kept, unlinked from the deleted account, for as long as the law
requires: subscriptions, purchases, entitlement grants, the credit wallet and its
transactions, affiliate commissions and withdrawals.

Session only: a request authenticated with an API key is rejected with `403`, whatever its
scopes. The request is refused with `409` while something could still charge the card or
while the user holds an unpaid affiliate balance:

- a subscription the billing provider still reports as active, on hold, past due or paused,
  or one created in the last 24 hours that is not paid yet: cancel it from Billing first. A
  subscription already set to cancel at the end of its period still blocks deletion until
  that period ends;
- `details.code: "CHECKOUT_IN_PROGRESS"`: a checkout session is open; finish or cancel it
  first;
- an affiliate withdrawal is requested or approved and not yet paid or rejected;
- `details.code: "AFFILIATE_BALANCE_FORFEIT"`: deleting forfeits the unpaid commissions in
  `details.amountCents` (`availableCents` plus `pendingCents`, in `currency`). Show the
  amount, then repeat the request with `confirmAffiliateForfeit: true` and
  `confirmedAffiliateForfeitCents` set to the amount shown. If the balance has grown past
  that amount, the request is refused again with the new one.

parameters.name: confirmAffiliateForfeit
parameters.description: Same as `confirmAffiliateForfeit` in the body, for clients that cannot send a body with `DELETE`.

The body is not valid JSON. The confirmation fields are read leniently, so a wrong value

balance that was not confirmed (`details.code: "AFFILIATE_BALANCE_FORFEIT"`, with
`amountCents`, `currency`, `availableCents` and `pendingCents`).

503.description:
Account deletion is temporarily unavailable: the checkout state could not be read, or the
sessions could not be revoked before the deletion. The account is untouched; try again
shortly. Also sent, with `details.code` `AUTH_UNAVAILABLE`, when the session store cannot
be read, and as "Service temporarily unavailable" when the database cannot be reached.

deletionUnavailable.summary: Checkout state unreadable, or sessions not revoked

value.message: Account deletion is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.

put.description:
Updates the display name of the authenticated user. Requires the `user:write` scope when
called with an API key.

The email address is read-only through this API. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed
before validation.

name.description: Name cannot be null or empty when updating.

400.description: Validation error. A body that is not valid JSON answers "Invalid JSON body".

invalidJson.summary: The body is not valid JSON

put.description:
Claims the authenticated user's username. Requires the `user:write` scope when called with an
API key.

The username is the public identifier in share-link URLs (`/share/{username}/{slug}`) and, for
accounts holding `custom_subdomain`, the published-portfolio subdomain — so a user cannot
create a share link until one is set.

**A username can only be set once.** Once the account has one, this endpoint rejects any
different value with `409 Username is locked and cannot be changed`. Re-sending the value the
account already holds is a no-op and returns `200`, so the call is safe to retry.

The submitted value is **normalised before validation**: lowercased, non-`[a-z0-9_-]`
characters folded to hyphens, leading/trailing hyphens stripped, and truncated to 32
characters. `Jane.Doe` and `jane-doe` therefore claim the same username. A value with no
letters, digits, `_` or `-` at all (such as `!!!`) normalises to `user` and claims that name
rather than being refused. The result must be 3 to 32 characters and must not be a reserved
word (`admin`, `api`, `app`, `docs`, and similar platform-owned names). Check with
`GET /users/{username}/availability` before committing.

A successful claim invalidates the caller's cached session so the new username is visible
immediately rather than at the end of the session-cache TTL.

username.description: Normalised server-side before the validity check runs.

400.description:
The username failed validation after normalisation. The detail message is the reason:
`too_short`, `invalid_characters` or `reserved`. A body that is not valid JSON answers
"Invalid JSON body".

documented.summary: The username is reserved

invalidJson.summary: The body is not valid JSON

409.description: The username is taken, or this account already has one.

locked.summary: This account already has a username

value.message: Username is locked and cannot be changed

put.description:
Turns the account-level background document sync on or off. Requires the `user:write` scope
when called with an API key.

This is the account-wide switch. It does not override a document's own `keepLocalOnly` flag —
a document opted out individually stays local even with auto-sync on. Turning auto-sync off
does not delete anything already synced; it only stops new local edits from being pushed.

Defaults to `true` on a new account. A successful change invalidates the caller's cached
session.

400.description: Validation error. A body that is not valid JSON answers "Invalid JSON body".

documented.summary: Validation error

invalidJson.summary: The body is not valid JSON

get.description:
Reports whether a username can be claimed. Intended to drive live feedback in a username
picker before `PUT /users/me/username` is called.

This route carries **no API-key scope gate**, unlike the rest of the Users module — but it is
still not anonymous, so it needs an API key or a whitelisted first-party origin.

The path segment is normalised the same way the update endpoint normalises it, and
`normalizedUsername` echoes back the value that would actually be stored. A `200` with
`available: false` is the normal negative answer — an unavailable name is not an error.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The candidate username. Normalised server-side before the lookup.

get.description:
Fetch aggregated issue and pull-request statistics for the configured repository, as of the
last sync. Served from the last synced snapshot, not live from GitHub — `syncedAt` tells you
how fresh it is. Cached for 12 hours.

This endpoint has no user session of its own: call it with an API key holding the
`github:read` scope, or from a whitelisted first-party origin. A request with neither is
rejected with `401`.

Fetch paginated GitHub issues and pull requests with optional filters, from the last synced
snapshot rather than live from GitHub. Ordered by most recently updated. Returns an empty
page when no sync has run yet.

Requires the `github:read` scope when called with an API key.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Derived at sync time — closed items and items labelled `done` map to `done`; items
labelled `in-progress`, `in progress`, or `active` map to `in-progress`; everything else
is `todo`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `all` is equivalent to omitting the filter.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page. Values above 50 are rejected with `400`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page index, the first page when left out. An alternative to `offset`: sending both answers `400` "Send either page or offset, not both".

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Alternative spelling of `limit`. Takes precedence over `limit` when both are sent.

parameters.name: createdFrom
parameters.description:
Items created at or after this time. A date (`2026-08-01`) means the start of that UTC
day; a date-time is used as given.

parameters.name: createdTo
parameters.description:
Items created at or before this time, inclusive. A bare date covers that whole UTC day, so
`createdTo=2026-08-10` includes everything up to `2026-08-11T00:00:00Z`.

parameters.name: updatedFrom
parameters.description: Items updated at or after this time. Same date rules as `createdFrom`.

parameters.name: updatedTo
parameters.description: Items updated at or before this time, inclusive. Same date rules as `createdTo`.

400.description:
Validation error: a parameter is out of range or not a date, `page` and `offset` were
both sent, or the query has a parameter this endpoint does not know (unknown parameters
are refused, not ignored).

details.message: Send either page or offset, not both

post.description:
Manually triggers a GitHub sync. **Administrators only** — the caller's session email must
match the configured `ADMIN_EMAIL`; an API key cannot reach this route.

Incremental by default: only issues updated since the last sync are refetched. The run is
guarded by a 10-minute Redis lock, so a concurrent attempt fails with `409` rather than
double-syncing.

A sync can take minutes, so it runs in the background: the response is `202` as soon as
the lock is taken. `GET /github/stats` shows the new `syncedAt` once it has finished; a
failed run leaves the previous data in place.

202.description: The sync started and is running in the background.

403.description: The authenticated user is not the configured administrator.

409.description: A sync is already running.

example.message: GitHub sync is already in progress

500.description: The server has no `ADMIN_EMAIL` set, so no one can be the administrator.

503.description:
The sync cannot start: Redis, which holds its lock, is unreachable, or
`GITHUB_OWNER`/`GITHUB_REPO` are not configured.

example.message: Syncing is unavailable right now. Try again shortly.

post.description:
Emails a one-time password to the given address.

Authentication is handled by **Better Auth**, mounted at `/api/v1/auth`. Its endpoints return
Better Auth's own payloads — they are **not** wrapped in the `{ success, message, data }`
envelope the rest of this API uses.

Rate limited to 10 requests per minute per IP, and to 5 codes per hour per email address
(`+tag` and Gmail dot variants of one inbox share that budget). The per-address limit
applies to `type: sign-in` and is checked before any mail is sent.

type.description:
Required. Use `sign-in` for the login flow — that is what the VeriWorkly
dashboard sends. For a password-reset code use Better Auth's
`/email-otp/request-password-reset`; the older `/forget-password/email-otp`
path is switched off.

200.description:
OTP sent. Returns `{ "success": true }` whether or not the address maps to an existing
account, so this endpoint cannot be used to enumerate registered emails.

400.description:
Missing or malformed body, an invalid email address, or `type: change-email`, which this
endpoint rejects. Returned in Better Auth's error shape, not `ErrorResponse`.

403.description: The request's `Origin` is not in the server's trusted origins.

429.description:
Too many OTP requests: 10 per minute per IP, or 5 per hour for this email address ("Too
many codes requested for this email. Please try again later."). Better Auth answers with
`{ "message": "..." }` and, for the per-IP limit, an `X-Retry-After` header. Outside
development the server's own limiter (20 requests per minute per IP for each
`/api/v1/auth/*` endpoint) can answer first, with `ErrorResponse` and a `Retry-After`
header. When the server cannot count requests it answers `503` instead of sending an
uncounted code.

503.description:
The server cannot count code requests right now (its rate-limit store is unreachable), so
it sends no code. Better Auth answers with `{ "message": "Sign-in codes are temporarily
unavailable. Please try again shortly." }`.

post.description:
Exchanges a valid OTP for a session. On success the session cookie is set via `Set-Cookie`
and the session token plus the user record are returned.

A user is created automatically on first sign-in. Codes expire after 5 minutes and allow 3
attempts by default. This endpoint returns Better Auth's payload, not the
`{ success, message, data }` envelope.

Rate limited to 20 requests per minute per IP. Guessing one code is bounded by the attempt
limit instead. Codes are 6 digits. The code lifetime and attempt count are the server's
`AUTH_OTP_TTL_SECONDS` (300) and `AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_ATTEMPTS` (3).

name.description: Used only when the account is created on this first sign-in.

image.description: Used only when the account is created on this first sign-in.

200.description: OTP verified. Sets the session cookie and returns the session token and user.

token.description: Session token for the authenticated session.

400.description:
The body is invalid, the code is wrong (`INVALID_OTP`), or it has expired
(`OTP_EXPIRED`). Returned in Better Auth's error shape, `{ code, message }`.

403.description:
The attempt limit was reached (`TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS`). The code is discarded, so request a
new one.

429.description: Too many requests. The limit is 20 per minute per IP, and Better Auth sends an `X-Retry-After` header.

get.description:
Returns the active session and its user, based on the request's session cookie. Returns
`null` rather than an error when no valid session cookie is present.

This endpoint returns Better Auth's payload, not the `{ success, message, data }` envelope.

200.description: The active `{ session, user }` pair, or `null` when the caller has no valid session.

post.description:
Revokes the current session and clears the session cookie. Also flushes the server-side
session cache for that cookie. It succeeds even when no session cookie is sent.

A request that carries a cookie must also send an `Origin` or `Referer` header from a trusted
origin, or it is rejected with `403`.

This endpoint returns Better Auth's payload, not the `{ success, message, data }` envelope.

200.description: Signed out. Clears the session cookie.

403.description: A cookie was sent without an `Origin` or `Referer` from a trusted origin.

get.description:
Lists the caller's API keys, newest first.

**No form of the secret is returned here — not even a masked one.** Each entry carries only
`keyPrefix`, the first 8 characters of the key, which is enough to tell keys apart in a list.
If you lose a secret, rotate the key.

Session-authenticated only — an API key cannot be used to manage API keys.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Keys per page. Read leniently: a value above 50 is lowered to 50, and a value that is not
a positive integer is ignored (the default applies). Neither is refused.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
Rows to skip. A value that is not a non-negative integer is ignored. An offset past row
1,000,000 is refused with `400`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
1-based page index, the first page when left out. An alternative to `offset`. When both
are sent, `offset` decides the window and the response echoes the `page` that was sent.
A value that is not a positive integer is ignored.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
Alternative spelling of `limit`, with the same lenient reading. Takes precedence over
`limit` when both are sent.

400.description: The requested window reaches past row 1,000,000.

post.description:
Generates a new API key. **The full secret is returned exactly once, in this response.** It
is stored only as an HMAC-SHA256 hash and can never be retrieved again — save it immediately.

Session-authenticated only — an API key cannot be used to mint API keys.

name.description: A descriptive name for the API key. Surrounding spaces are trimmed.

scopes.description:
Scopes granted to the new key. Defaults to `["user:read"]` (the server's
`API_KEY_DEFAULT_SCOPES`) when omitted, empty, or an empty string. A comma-separated string such as
`"user:read,resume:read"` is also accepted. Any value outside the listed set is
rejected with `400`.

rateLimit.description:
Requests allowed per 15-minute window. Defaults to 20 (the server's
`API_KEY_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT`). The ceiling is `API_KEY_MAX_RATE_LIMIT`, 600 by
default: a larger value is lowered to the ceiling, not rejected. A numeric string
such as `"50"` is accepted. A value that is not a positive integer is rejected
with `400`.

get.description:
Lists the authenticated user's documents (resumes, cover letters, portfolios, link-in-bio
pages), optionally filtered by type. Soft-deleted documents are excluded. Document bodies
are left out unless `includeContent=true`.

**Paging.** Every response is one page: `limit` documents, 20 when it is not sent. To read
the whole list, send each page's `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is `null`. `total`
is the number of live documents of this type. Send the same
`type`, `updatedSince` and `includeContent` on every page of one walk; a cursor that was
not issued for them is rejected with `400` and `details.code` `INVALID_DOCUMENT_CURSOR`.

- The plain list goes newest first, by `updatedAt` then `id`.
- A sync walk (`updatedSince` set, or `includeContent=true`) goes oldest first, by
  `updatedAt` then `id`. A document edited during the walk comes back again on a later
  page, so none is skipped; keep the copy you saw last.
- With `updatedSince`, documents deleted since then come back in `deleted`, also paged
  (up to `limit` per page, oldest deletion first) beside the documents. Keep following
  `nextCursor` until it is `null`.
- Every page of one walk repeats the first page's `serverTime`. Use it as the next
  `updatedSince` only after the last page.

A request without `limit` used to get one unpaged list of up to 500 documents; it now gets
the first page of 20, with `nextCursor`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Documents per page, 20 by default, at most 50, or at most 20 with `includeContent=true` (a larger value is rejected with `400`).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The previous page's `nextCursor`, unchanged. Opaque; do not build or edit it.

dropped, so a `202` does not guarantee the count increased.

whitelisted first-party origin; otherwise it is rejected with `401`.

published portfolio's subdomain can send it without a preflight. A `text/plain` body is
limited to 5 KB and is read before the credential check, so an oversized one gets `413`
even without a key; a JSON body falls under the 100 kb default.

are still accepted with `202`. A Redis failure while buffering answers `500`.

body may be at most 4 MB. It is not echoed in the response, nor in the owner's list of
links.

Replacing an existing link without it keeps the stored value. It is a display preference,
not a security control: the studio hides the Download button, and viewers can still save
the page.

`allowDownload` says whether to show a Download button. It is a display preference, not a

post.description:

the stored scrypt hash, and returns the full snapshot on success.

No user session is required, but the request must carry an API key or originate from a
whitelisted first-party origin, same as the read endpoint.

**Rate limited to 5 password attempts per link per 5 minutes per client network**, and to 20
requests per 5 minutes per IP across all links, to make these links impractical to

window. The code is matched case-insensitively.
Entire affiliate program is gated behind a feature flag (`config.growth.affiliateProgramEnabled`)
that defaults off in production until explicitly enabled — every route in this group,

get.description:

Public callers may send only the allow-listed event names listed under `event`, and every

reported. Trusted servers send `x-internal-key` instead of an API key, which also allows any
other name, stored as `custom_<name>` (at most 50 distinct custom names per UTC day), and a
`value` up to 1000.

parameters.name: x-internal-key
parameters.description: Server-to-server secret (`STATS_INTERNAL_KEY`). Never sent from a browser.

400.description: The body is invalid, or the event name is not allow-listed for public callers. A body that is not valid JSON answers "Invalid JSON body".

429.description: Rate limited, or an internal caller sent a new custom name past the daily cap. The per-IP limit also answers `429` ("Too many requests. Please try again later."). With an API key, the per-key limit (20 requests per 15 minutes by default) also answers `429`.

value.message: Too many requests. Please try again later.
Rate limit exceeded. You are allowed 20 requests per 15 minutes. Please try again in 840 seconds.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description:
Your personal API key — `vw_` followed by 64 hex characters. The same key is also accepted
as `Authorization: Bearer vw_...`.

LocalSession.name: veriworkly-auth.session_token
LocalSession.description: Internal session cookie for local development.

details.description:
Left out when there is nothing to add. A validation failure (`400` "Validation failed")
sends an array of `{ path, message }`, one entry per rejected field. Other errors send an
object instead, such as `{ code }`, `{ currentUpdatedAt }` or the caller's quota. Each
operation's error responses say which.

UnauthorizedResponse.description:
The body of a `401`. It has the same envelope as every other error, so `statusCode` is always
present. When the gate in front of a key-or-session route refuses the request, it names the
reason in `details.code`. An invalid API key and a missing session on a signed-in-only route
send no `details`.

code.description:
`API_KEY_REQUIRED`: no API key and no whitelisted first-party `Origin` or `Referer`.
`AUTH_REQUIRED`: a session cookie with no `Origin` or `Referer` that is not a valid
session.

AtsQuotaErrorResponse.description: The body of a `429` from the ATS quota, where `details` is the caller's current quota. A `429` from the rate limiters has no `details`.

OffsetPaginationMeta.description:
Offset-pagination metadata returned alongside `items` by every paginated list endpoint.
Requests may use either `page`/`pageSize` or `limit`/`offset`; the response always echoes both
views of the same window.

total.description: Total number of matching records, ignoring the current window.

page.description: 1-based page index for the current window.

nextCursor.description: Always null — these endpoints are offset-paginated, never cursor-paginated.

HealthLivenessData.description:
Liveness payload. `GET /api/v1/health` deliberately touches no external dependency, so uptime
checks do not wake database compute — it reports only that the Node.js process is responding.

HealthReadyData.description: Readiness payload. Only `GET /api/v1/health/ready` verifies PostgreSQL and Redis connectivity.

username.description:
Null until the user claims one. Immutable once set, and required before any share link can
be created.

_count.description: Relational counts for the user's own records.

apiKeys.description: Every API key on the account, active, revoked or expired.

shareLinks.description: Share links on documents that are not deleted, as the share list counts them.

resumes.description:
The documents list's count: documents that are not deleted, of every type except
`PORTFOLIO`.

normalizedUsername.description: The value that would actually be stored, after server-side normalisation.

reason.description:
Present only when `available` is `false`. The path segment is cut to 32 characters during
normalisation, so a long name is never refused for length. A value with no letters,
digits, `_` or `-` normalises to `user`.

shareResumeCount.description: The user's share links on documents that are not deleted, as the share list counts them.

MasterProfileItemId.description: Client-generated id, unique within its list. Surrounding spaces are trimmed.

MasterProfileMonthDate.description: `YYYY-MM`, or an empty string when not known.

MasterProfileYearDate.description: `YYYY`, or an empty string when not known.

MasterProfileUrl.description: An `http://` or `https://` URL, or an empty string.

MasterProfileEmail.description: A valid email address, or an empty string when not provided.

MasterProfilePhone.description:
Empty when not provided. Otherwise either a number that starts with `+` and the country code
and is valid for that country (`"+14155550123"`, `"+1 (415) 555-0123"`), or 7 to 15 digits
with nothing else (`"9876543210"`, kept for numbers saved before country codes were
collected). `"(987) 654-3210"` is rejected. The value is stored as sent.

referenceId.description: The credential id printed on the certificate.

date.description: Free text. Not checked against a date format.

link.description: Free text. Not checked as a URL.

customSectionId.description: The id of the custom section this entry orders and shows or hides. Set only when `id` is `custom`.

MasterProfileContent.description:
The resume-shaped JSON stored in `MasterProfile.content`.

On `PUT /profiles/master`, `templateId`, `basics`, `links`, `summary` and `customization` are
required. An omitted array is stored as `[]`, and keys not listed here are dropped rather than
rejected. Inside an item, every property is required unless its schema marks it optional.
Every array item carries a client-generated `id`. Each top-level array holds at most 200
items. A payload larger than 1 MB once serialized is rejected with `413`.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the profile content format. Defaults to the current version when omitted.

expectedUpdatedAt.description:
The `updatedAt` from your last read. Leave it out only when the profile has never been
saved; a save over an existing profile without it is rejected with `409`. `null` is
rejected with `400`.

isPaid.description: The caller has any plan (AI Credits, Creator Pro or the Job Hunter Bundle) or a pass. A credit pack does not count.

unlimited.description: True for a paid caller's LinkedIn quota. `remaining` and `limit` are then null.

limit.description: 1 for a free caller (a day for GitHub, 30 days for LinkedIn), 50 a day for a paid caller's GitHub imports, null when unlimited.

connectedUsername.description: The GitHub login of the linked account, read from GitHub for a free caller. Null for a paid caller, for LinkedIn, or when GitHub cannot be reached.

hasGithubAccount.description: GitHub quota only. A GitHub login is linked to the account, whatever GitHub says about its token.

usernameOrUrl.description:
A GitHub username or profile URL. Always required and checked (`400` when it is neither).
Free users may only import their own OAuth-connected account, so for them the linked
GitHub login is imported instead of this value; paid users may import any public username.

replaceMaster.description: When true, also overwrites the user's master profile with the imported content.

profileText.description: Raw copy-pasted text from a LinkedIn profile export or PDF (parsed by AI, not fetched via any LinkedIn API).

replaceMaster.description: When true, also overwrites the user's master profile with the imported content.

requestId.description:
The client's id for this import, as on every other AI route. A retry with the same id,
the same text and the same `replaceMaster` after a lost response returns the document
already created (`replayed: true`) without charging again; the same id with different
text or a different `replaceMaster` is `409`.

data.description:
The newly created resume Document seeded from the imported data. A LinkedIn import
replayed by `requestId` returns the stored document with `replayed: true` added.

replayed.description: Present and `true` only on a LinkedIn import replayed by `requestId`.

ChangelogPrRef.description: A pull request referenced by a changelog entry, resolved from the GitHub release body.

version.description: Semantic version string, unique across entries.

ChangelogEntryDetail.description: A single entry, with the row's timestamps the list leaves out.

editedAt.description: When an admin last edited the entry, or `null` if only the release sync wrote it.

latest.description: The most recently published entry, or `null` when the changelog is empty.

contributorCount.description:
Distinct contributors, counted once each by GitHub login: the core team, the repository's
contributors from the last GitHub sync, the pull-request authors on every entry, and
`@mentions` in entry text.

topContributors.description: Up to 30 of the contributors counted in `contributorCount`, the core team first, then in the order they were found. Not ranked by contributions.

totalItems.description: The same value as `total`, kept for older clients.

completionRate.description: Percentage of `total` that is done, formatted to 2 decimal places. `"0.00"` when there is nothing synced.

nextSyncAt.description: When the next scheduled sync is due.

data.description: Null until the first GitHub sync has run for the configured repository.

syncedAt.description: When the snapshot was taken, or `null` before the first sync.

NullDataResponse.description: Success envelope for endpoints that acknowledge an action without returning a body.

ApiKeyScope.description:
API key scopes are a fixed set — requesting any other value fails with `400`. Each scope maps
to the `requireApiKeyScopes(...)` gate on the corresponding routes. Scope checks apply only to
API-key callers; session callers are not scope-gated.

ApiKeyListItem.description:
The trimmed shape returned by `GET /api-keys`. The secret is **not** included in any form —
not even masked. Use `keyPrefix` to identify a key in a list.

keyPrefix.description: First 8 characters of the key (`vw_` plus 5 hex characters).

lastUsed.description: Written at most once every 5 minutes per key, so it lags real usage slightly.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working. With `revokedAt`, this tells an expired key from a revoked one.

revokedAt.description: When the key was revoked, by the user or by a rotation, or `null`.

ApiKeySecret.description:
Returned only by `POST /api-keys` and `POST /api-keys/{id}/rotate`. `key` is the full secret
and is shown exactly once — it is stored only as an HMAC-SHA256 hash and cannot be retrieved
again.

key.description: The full secret — `vw_` followed by 64 hex characters. Shown once, never again.

rateLimit.description: Requests allowed per 15-minute window for this key.

expiresAt.description: Always set. Defaults to 365 days from creation when not supplied.

rotatedFromId.description: Only present on a rotate response — the id of the key this one replaced.

ApiKeyDetail.description:
The full metadata record for a single key, returned by `GET /api-keys/{id}`. Identical to
`ApiKeySecret` minus `key` — the secret itself is unrecoverable after creation.

keySuffix.description: Last 8 characters of the key. Not enough to reconstruct the secret.

rateLimit.description: Requests allowed per 15-minute window for this key.

lastUsed.description: Written at most once every 5 minutes per key, so it lags real usage slightly.

slug.description: Unique per user. Also used as the portfolio subdomain slug for PORTFOLIO documents.

content.description: Document-type-specific JSON payload (resume schema, portfolio schema, etc).

revision.description: Incremented on every update. Required (and checked) on PATCH for optimistic concurrency control.

deletedAt.description: Set by soft delete. Documents with a non-null deletedAt are excluded from list/get.

portfolioSubdomain.description: A PORTFOLIO draft's chosen subdomain; `null` on every other type.

moderatedPrivateAt.description:
When a moderator made the document private. While set, the owner cannot share it or make
it anything but `PRIVATE`.

DocumentListResponse.description: One page of the list, `limit` documents (20 by default). Follow `nextCursor` for the rest.

serverTime.description:
The server's clock when the walk started, the same on every page of one walk. Send it as
the next `updatedSince` once the last page has been read.

deleted.description: Documents deleted at or after `updatedSince` (empty without it). Paged like `data`.

nextCursor.description: Send as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

total.description: The user's live documents of the requested type, whatever `updatedSince` says.

DocumentListErrorResponse.description:
A `400` from the document list: `details` is the failing fields for a validation error, or
`{ code: "INVALID_DOCUMENT_CURSOR" }` for a bad cursor.

DocumentSummary.description:
A document as the list endpoint returns it. Carries no `userId`, `schemaVersion` or
`deletedAt`, and carries `content` only when the request sets `includeContent=true`.

DocumentUpdateResult.description:
The updated document without `content` and `metadata`: an update sends the whole body, so it
is not echoed back. `GET /documents/{id}` returns them.

revision.description: The new revision. Send it with the next update.

portfolioSubdomain.description: A PORTFOLIO draft's chosen subdomain; `null` on every other type.

moderatedPrivateAt.description: When a moderator made the document private, or `null`.

id.description:
Optional client-generated id: 1 to 64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`. If the caller already
has a live document with this id, it is returned as-is (idempotent create). An id another
account uses is `409` "Document ID already in use"; one of the caller's documents in the
trash is `409` "Document was deleted".

slug.description: Normalised to a URL slug before it is stored.

content.description: If omitted for RESUME/COVER_LETTER, content is auto-seeded from the user's MasterProfile when one exists.

slug.description: Normalised to a URL slug before it is stored.

updateShareSlug.description: When true and an active share link exists, its slug is updated to track the new document slug.

revision.description: Must match the document's current revision. Mismatch returns 409.

AtsCategory.description:
The rule category. Integrity checks (hidden text, instructions aimed at an AI screener, a
copied posting, keyword stuffing) deduct their impact from the score in points rather than
weighing in its denominator.

evidence.description: What was found, quoted where it can be.

scoreImpact.description: The weight the rule cost here (for an integrity rule, the points deducted). 0 when passed.

AtsKeywordGroups.description: Posting terms by kind, each group at most 12. Soft skills weigh less in `jobMatchScore`.

AtsAdvice.description:
Something worth knowing that is not scored: the file (name, size, password, tracked
changes), details that can invite age bias where the region asks, and notes about a named
applicant tracking system. Never part of the score, the categories, the failed checks or the
fixes.

evidence.description: What was found, quoted. Absent when there is nothing to quote.

source.description: For an `ats` note, the vendor's public page that documents it.

AtsReport.description:
Deterministic, rule-based ATS report. Computed entirely server-side without calling any AI
model. Shape depends on the caller's auth state: anonymous requests to `/ats/check` get
`AtsRestrictedReport` (scores, verdict and counts); any signed-in caller (free or paid) gets
`AtsFullReport`. `/ats/analyze` requires a signed-in caller and always returns
`AtsFullReport`.

AtsFullReport.description: Full deterministic report — every rule's evidence, all matched/missing keywords, all prioritized fixes. Requires a signed-in caller.

matchedKeywords.description: Posting terms the resume has, hard skills first, then soft.

missingKeywords.description: Posting terms the resume lacks, hard skills first, then soft.

keywordCounts.description: How many posting terms the resume has and lacks, past the 12 the lists show.

parsingWarnings.description:
Every failed check that stops an ATS reading the document, then a note when the resume
was cut at 50,000 characters, when the job posting was cut at 20,000 characters, and
when the posting lists more than the 25 requirements that are judged.

checksPassed.description: Number of deterministic rules the resume passed.

checksTotal.description: Total number of deterministic rules evaluated.

wordCount.description: Words counted in the extracted resume text.

locale.description:
What the resume (and posting) were read as: the language packs used beyond the base
vocabulary, and the region applied (from a +country-code phone number, else the
language's usual country). Regions set phone and date conventions and weigh
country-specific checks such as a stated date of birth or a photo.

unsupported.description:
The language the resume is written in when no pack reads it: an ISO 639 code
(`it`), a script (`Cyrillic`), or `und`. A parsing warning says so. Null otherwise.

engine.description:
What produced the report. The same input, reference date, engine version and policy
fingerprint always give the same report.

policy.description: The policy's declared version and a hash of its content as applied, locale packs included.

requirements.description: The job posting's requirements, each judged against the resume. Empty without a job description.

AtsRequirement.description:
One requirement of the posting, as a per-qualification screener grades it. `unverifiable`
means the resume cannot settle it — the right to work, a clearance — unless it states it.

text.description: The requirement as the posting wrote it.

kind.description: `seniority` is the level named in the job title, such as Senior. It comes first when there is one.

terms.description: What the requirement names, and whether the resume has each. Skills and languages.

evidence.description: Resume lines that show it, quoted. Work history first, a skills list last.

detail.description: For years, degrees, language levels and clearances, what was compared.
detail.example: 6 years in the work history, 5 asked

AtsCategoryScore.description:
Per-area rollup of the deterministic rules, saying which part of the resume is losing points
without revealing which rule fired or what it weighs. Signed-in callers only — the rollup
carries most of the diagnostic value, so it is not part of the anonymous shape.

score.description: Percentage of this category's own weight the resume kept (0-100).

passed.description: Rules in this category that passed.

possible.description: Worst-case points this category could have cost.

AtsRestrictedReport.description:
Returned instead of AtsFullReport when /ats/check is called anonymously. A diagnosis without
the prescription: scores, a verdict, the single most serious problem and the single
highest-impact fix stated in full, plus honest counts of everything withheld. No per-area
rollup, no rule evidence, no keyword lists, and no recovered work history — the server never
sends them, so there is nothing for a client to un-hide.

topFix.description: The single highest-impact fix, in full. The rest of the list requires a signed-in caller.

primaryWarning.description:
The most serious parsing or formatting failure, phrased as the risk it creates. Structural
failures outrank heavier content ones here because a candidate cannot self-diagnose them:
a missing keyword is visible by reading the posting, a column layout that scrambles your
job titles on extraction is not.

matchedKeywordCount.description: How many job-description terms the resume covers. The terms themselves require a signed-in caller.

missingKeywordCount.description: How many job-description terms the resume is missing. The terms themselves require a signed-in caller.

parsedRoleCount.description: How many work-history rows were recovered. The rows themselves require a signed-in caller.

remainingFixCount.description: Prioritised fixes beyond the one shown.

advice.description: Each piece of advice as its id, kind and message. The evidence, fix and source stay in the full report.

AtsAiInsights.description: Null when the AI step was skipped (e.g. `/check`, which never calls AI).

tier.description: subscriber: spendable AI credits from any source, or a subscription or pass in effect even with an empty wallet (a paying customer is never free). paused: a paused subscription and no credits; the free limits apply. free: any other signed-in account, including one whose payment failed.

limit.description: 1 for anonymous callers per 48h window, 2 for free and paused logged-in users per 24h window, 300 for subscribers per billing period.

canConvertResume.description:
True when the caller's credit balance (from any source) covers a resume conversion
(`/ats/convert-resume`). False when `pricing` is null.

canRepair.description:
True when this deployment offers the AI parse repair (`repairParse` on `/ats/analyze`)
and the caller's credit balance covers it. Offer repair only when this is true.

pricing.description:
Credit prices of the ATS AI actions. Null when the server could not load its ATS AI
settings; conversion and repair are then off.

parseRepairCredits.description:
Credits charged by the optional AI parse repair (`repairParse` on `/ats/analyze`),
on top of the analysis. `null` when this deployment does not offer repair.

extract.description: Separate budget for resume file uploads (POST /ats/extract) — does not share the scan quota above.

AtsParsedResume.description:
The fields an applicant tracking system recovers from the document — the "what the ATS sees"
view. Produced by the same deterministic pass as the scores, so it never costs a second scan.
A blank employer or a missing date range is a column a recruiter's filter cannot match on,
which is why the rows are returned verbatim rather than only summarised.

roles.description: One row per job, in the shape an ATS stores it.

isced.description: The ISCED 2011 level of the credential — 3 upper secondary (Abitur, Class XII), 6 bachelor's or equivalent, 7 master's or equivalent (a German Diplom), 8 doctoral.

certifications.description: Certifications and licences, from their own section or a "Certifications:" line.

spokenLanguages.description: Languages spoken, each once. Programming languages stay in `skills`.

level.description: The level as written, such as `native`. Empty when none was given.

cefr.description: The CEFR level, or null when no known level word was given.

monthsOfExperience.description: Calendar months covered by at least one role, so overlapping jobs are counted once.

highestIsced.description: The highest ISCED 2011 level among the education entries.

provenance.description:
Where each group of fields came from. `parser` was read from the text by the deterministic
parser — what an ATS would see. `structured` was taken from the typed fields of an
`AtsResumeDocument` or a JSON Resume. `ai` was recovered by the optional parse repair and
grounded against the text. `none` means nothing was recovered.

AtsResumeInput.description:
The resume, in any of three shapes:

- **Text** — extracted from a file or pasted. Parsed deterministically.
- **`AtsResumeDocument`** — structured data, identified by `format: "ats-resume@1"`. The ATS
  record is read from its fields; the content checks run on its rendered text. An invalid
  document is rejected with 400 before any quota is consumed.
- **JSON Resume** (jsonresume.org) — recognised by shape and read the same way as a document.
  One that exceeds the document limits is scored as flattened text instead.

Any other object is flattened to text, keys on their own lines.

oneOf.description: Trimmed first; it must not be empty after trimming.

AtsResumeDocument.description:
A resume as structured data. Dates are `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY`. Sections are in page order;
leave out hidden ones. `title` is the heading as printed, in the resume's own language.

month.description: Null when the resume gave only a year.

AtsLayoutSignals.description:
Page geometry measured while parsing an uploaded document, for the format checks that text
alone cannot answer. Returned by `POST /ats/extract` and accepted back by `/ats/check` and
`/ats/analyze`. When it is omitted, the rules that depend on it are left out of the report
entirely — neither passed nor failed — and out of the score's denominator.

A count above its bound is held at the bound rather than rejected: 500 for `tableCount` and
`imageCount`, 200 for `pageCount` and `imageOnlyPages`, 100,000 for `hiddenTextChars`,
`trackedChanges` and `comments`.

columnRatio.description: Share of content lines split across a horizontal gutter — the signature of a two-column layout, sidebar, or floating text box, all of which extract in a scrambled reading order. Null when the document had too few content lines for the measurement to carry signal.

tableCount.description: Number of ruled table grids found by tracing the page's vector drawing operators.

imageCount.description: Images printed at least 50pt a side and smaller than half the page — most likely a photo. Absent when not measured, which leaves the photo check out of the report.

hiddenTextChars.description:
Characters an ATS reads but a reader cannot see — in the background's colour or close to
it, under 2pt, off the page, invisible, transparent, or covered by an image. The OCR text
layer of a scan is not counted. Feeds the integrity check `ats-v2.integrity.hiddenText`.

hiddenText.description: All of that hidden text, whitespace collapsed, cut to 5,000 characters.

hiddenTextRead.description: The part of `hiddenText` that the document's text also holds, which is what an ATS reads.

imageOnlyPages.description: Pages that are an image with no text layer — a scan, or a page saved as a picture.

metadataText.description: The file's title, subject, keywords and author. Never scored as resume text; read only for instructions aimed at an AI screener.

encrypted.description: A PDF that opened without a password but is encrypted. Read by the advice only, never the score.

trackedChanges.description: Tracked changes still in a Word document. Read by the advice only, never the score.

comments.description: Comments still in a Word document. Read by the advice only, never the score.

text.description: Plain text extracted from the uploaded PDF, DOCX, HTML, TXT, Markdown, or JSON resume file (max ~50,000 characters).

AtsFileInfo.description: The uploaded file's name and size, sent back by the client for the file advice. Never scored.

jobDescription.description: Optional plain-text job description to compute a jobMatchScore against. Surrounding spaces are trimmed.

jobUrl.description: Required when fetchJobUrl is true. Fetched server-side through an SSRF-hardened HTTPS-only fetcher (blocks localhost/private/link-local IPs, pins the resolved IP for the whole request, caps redirects to 3 and response size to 2MB; the page may go 8s without sending data and must finish within 15s).

requestId.description: Client-generated idempotency key for the underlying AI credit reservation.

file.description: Accepted for parity with `/ats/check`, but not read by this endpoint.

repairParse.description:
Opt in to the AI parse-repair pass. It runs only when this is true **and** the
deterministic parse came back thin (`repair.available` in the response), and it spends
credits separately from the analysis. Every value the model returns must occur in the
resume text; values that do not are dropped and counted in `repair.rejectedValues`.
Spends AI credits from any source (a plan, a pass or a credit pack).

data.description:
AI insights are drawn from the same shared ATS scan-quota bucket consumed by `/ats/check` —
there is only one ATS quota, not separate "scan" and "AI" allowances.

aiStatus.description:
`unavailable` means no model could be routed for this request — a server-side
configuration problem, not a bad request. The deterministic report is still returned,
`ai` is null, no credits are charged, and the scan quota unit is refunded, so
`quota` reflects the balance after the refund.

replayed.description:
Present and `true` only when this is the stored answer to an earlier request with the
same `requestId` and input. Nothing is charged again, and `quota` is the current one.

AtsRepairSummary.description:
Outcome of the optional AI parse-repair pass. Present on every analyze response, whether or
not repair was requested, so a client can offer it when it would help.

available.description: The deterministic parse was thin enough that a repair pass would likely help.

applied.description: Repair ran and filled at least one field.

fields.description:
Fields in `report.parsed` supplied by the model rather than the deterministic parser.
Repair only ever fills fields the parser left empty; it never overwrites one.

rejectedValues.description: Values the model returned that do not occur in the resume and were dropped.

creditsSpent.description: Credits spent on repair, in addition to the analysis `creditsSpent`.

unusable.description: Repair ran but the model's answer could not be used. Nothing was filled and nothing was charged for it.

resume.description: Raw resume text to convert into structured JSON Resume fields.

AtsConvertedResume.description: AI-extracted resume fields. Every field defaults to an empty string/array when not explicitly present in the source text — nothing is invented.

creditsSpent.description:
Credits spent on the conversion. They come from any source (a plan, a pass or a credit
pack), independently of the shared ATS scan quota. A replay reports the conversion's
price here although nothing is charged again.

replayed.description:
Present and `true` only when this is the stored answer to an earlier request with the
same `requestId` and resume text.

data.description:
Map of AI action key to its credit cost per mode, containing an entry for every action in
`AiActionKey`. The values below are illustrative only — real costs come from server-side
configuration, so read them from this endpoint rather than hardcoding them.

mode.description: Expert mode uses a stronger model at a higher credit cost.

input.description:
Required, though every field inside it is optional and defaults to an empty string. At
least one of `text`, `context`, or `jobDescription` must be non-empty or the request fails
with `400`. Each action also has its own limits for `text` and `context`, set in the
server's AI policy and not published: over one, the request fails with `400` "Text
exceeds the N character limit." (or "Context exceeds…"), naming the limit. A
`jobDescription` over its action's limit is cut to that length, not refused.

jobDescription.description: Silently truncated to the action's own job-description limit rather than rejected.

requestId.description: Client-generated idempotency key. Credits are reserved against this id before generation and only committed on success — a failed or errored generation releases the reservation instead of spending credits.

documentId.description: Optional document to associate the credit transaction with.

balance.description: AI credit wallet balance after this generation.

replayed.description:
Present and `true` only when this is the stored answer to an earlier request with the
same `requestId` and input. Nothing is charged again.

PortfolioPublication.description:
A published portfolio as the public site reads it. The billing state behind it (live, in
grace) is not shown.

isPaid.description:
The owner's paid portfolio access (Creator Pro, the Job Hunter Bundle, a pass) is in
effect, or its short grace period after a lapse is still running. It decides the badge,
the custom subdomain and the extra pages on any template. An AI Credits plan alone does not
count.

isPremiumTemplate.description: The template is a premium one (`nimbus` or `cipher`). About the template only.

isPremium.description: `isPaid` and `isPremiumTemplate` both true. Kept for renderers that have not moved to the two fields.

PortfolioPublicationRecord.description:
The stored publication row as the owner sees it. This is a different shape from the public read
endpoint: it exposes the owner-only bookkeeping columns and has no `isPremium`.

suspensionReason.description:
Why the portfolio is suspended: `user_unpublished`, `grace_expired`, a billing status
(`ACTIVE`, `PAST_DUE`, `CANCELED` or `INACTIVE`) recorded by the billing job, or
`moderation:<reason>` for a moderator's takedown.

reasonBeforeModeration.description: The owner's or billing's own suspension reason that a moderator's takedown covers, restored when it is lifted; `null` when the site was online as the takedown went on.

firstPublishedAt.description: When the portfolio first went online. A republish moves `publishedAt`, not this.

publicUrl.description:
`https://{subdomain}.veriworkly.com` in production, or
`http://{subdomain}.localhost:3004` in development. Added by the publish endpoint
only — it is not a stored column.

data.description:
The updated publication record with `status: SUSPENDED`. Never null: a caller who never
published gets `404`. No `publicUrl` is included.

PortfolioDraft.description:
A trimmed projection of the caller's PORTFOLIO-type Document — not a full `Document`. Only the
fields below are selected.

slug.description:
The subdomain the draft was last saved under. It is not the document's own slug: a rename or
another document's slug never changes or blocks it. A PORTFOLIO document never saved as a
draft shows its document slug.

templateId.description:
`signal`, `atelier`, `nimbus` or `cipher` once the draft has been saved through
`PUT /portfolios/draft`. A PORTFOLIO document created through `/documents` and never saved
as a draft keeps the template it was created with (`modern` by default).

revision.description: Send this back as `revision` when saving or publishing.

templateId.description:
`signal`, `atelier`, `nimbus` or `cipher` once the draft has been saved through
`PUT /portfolios/draft`. A PORTFOLIO document created through `/documents` and never saved
as a draft keeps the template it was created with (`modern` by default).

draft.description: Null when the caller has never saved a portfolio draft.

billing.description: Same shape as the Billing "/billing/me" response.

PortfolioAssetReference.description: An image uploaded through `/portfolio-assets`. Publishing refuses an image that is not one of the owner's finished uploads.

title.description: Required to be non-empty on publish. A draft may leave it empty.

items.description: The section's entries. Their fields depend on the section type and are not checked by the server.

PortfolioDraftContent.description:
The portfolio content a draft stores and a publish serves. Saving a draft accepts empty
values where noted, so an unfinished portfolio can be kept. Publishing checks the stored draft
again with the stricter rules (a non-empty `identity.name`, `headline`, `bio` and a valid
`email`; every social link with a label and URL; every section and page with a title) and
answers `400` "Complete the required portfolio details before publishing." with the fields in
`details` otherwise. Surrounding spaces in text fields are trimmed.

templateId.description: `nimbus` and `cipher` are premium: publishing them needs Creator Pro, the Job Hunter Bundle or a pass.

name.description: Required to be non-empty on publish.

headline.description: Required to be non-empty on publish.

bio.description: Required to be non-empty on publish.

email.description: A valid email address. A draft may leave it empty; publishing needs one.

label.description: Required to be non-empty on publish.

url.description: An `http://` or `https://` URL. A draft may leave it empty; publishing needs one.

pages.description: Extra pages. The public site shows them only while the owner has paid portfolio access (`isPaid` on the public read).

title.description: Required to be non-empty on publish.

documentId.description: Omit to create (or continue) the user's single PORTFOLIO document.

revision.description: Required once a draft already exists, for optimistic concurrency (409 on mismatch).
Must match the draft's current revision (save the latest draft first).

locked.description:
True when the caller has no visitor-analytics access (it comes with Creator Pro, the Job
Hunter Bundle or a pass). The numbers are then all zero and the lists empty, whether or
not a portfolio is published.

totalViews.description: All-time views, including views still buffered and not yet flushed.

daily.description: The 30 most recent days that had views, newest first. Days with no views are left out.

referrers.description: The all-time top 10 referrer hosts, from flushed views only.

mimeType.description:
`image/jpeg`, `image/png` or `image/webp`. Checked by the service rather than the
request schema, so any other value answers `400` "Upload a JPG, PNG, or WebP image.".

sizeBytes.description:
Greater than 0 and at most 5,242,880 (5 MB). A larger size answers `400` "Image must be
5 MB or smaller.".

uploadUrl.description: Presigned Cloudflare R2 PUT URL. Upload the file directly to this URL with a matching Content-Type/Content-Length.

checksum.description: Optional ETag to verify against the uploaded object.

url.description:
Public CDN URL. Only returned after a server-side HEAD request against R2 confirms the
uploaded object's size, content type, and (optionally) checksum match what was declared
when the upload URL was requested.

plan.description: The plan whose features are in effect, from subscription or pass access. A credit pack unlocks no plan features, so a customer whose only purchase is a pack is FREE here although they paid; use `access` to tell a paying customer from a free one.

status.description:
Status of the subscription in effect today. `INACTIVE` when none is (no plan, or one that
has ended); `PAST_DUE` while a failed renewal's grace runs, or while the subscription is
paused. There are no trials.

interval.description:
The stored billing interval, upper case. Request bodies (checkout, plan change) use the
lower-case spelling (`monthly`, `annual`, ...).

graceEndsAt.description: When the grace period after a failed renewal ends. Null when none is running.

canPublish.description: Portfolio-publish entitlement is a separate system from the AI credit wallet below.

accessEndsAt.description: The latest period end of an active Creator Pro or Job Hunter Bundle subscription.

publicationStatus.description: `LIVE` while publishing is included, `GRACE` while a grace period runs, `SUSPENDED` otherwise.

access.description:
Who the customer is, separately from the plan. A payer is never shown as free: a customer
whose renewal failed, or who paused, keeps the tier of the subscription they pay for.

tier.description: `credits` is a customer whose only purchase is credits (a pack, or a plan allowance that is still unspent).

isPaid.description: A subscription, a pass or an admin grant of one is in effect. A credit pack never makes an account paid.

isPaying.description: The customer paid for something now in effect (a subscription, a pass, or paid credits), or has a subscription in dunning.

paymentIssue.description: A subscription renewal failed and is being retried. False for a pause.

catalog.description: The public product catalog, one entry per subscription product.

prices.description: Price in cents per interval (`one_day`, `seven_day`, `monthly`, `annual`) the product is sold in.

creditAllowance.description: AI credits granted per interval, for products that include them.

creditNotes.description: How the allowance is delivered, per interval, in words a pricing page can show.

configuredIntervals.description: The intervals that have a provider product configured on this server, so can be bought now.

addOns.description: What can be bought on top of portfolio access. Empty without it.

productName.description: What the event was for, as the customer knows it, such as `7-Day Hunt Pass`.

balance.description: The ledger balance. It can still hold credits that expired and were not yet swept; use `available` for what can be spent.

reserved.description: Credits currently held by in-flight AI generations that have not yet committed or been released.

available.description: Credits that can be spent now.

amount.description: Signed change to the balance. Negative for a debit or an expiry.

action.description: The AI action the credits were spent on, when there was one.

productKey.description: Validated against a fixed product/interval whitelist before being handed off to the Dodo Payments checkout API.

redirectUrl.description: Relative path (must start with a single `/`) to return to after checkout.

url.description: Dodo Payments hosted checkout URL to redirect the user to.

reused.description: True when an open checkout session for the same choice was handed back instead of a new one.

cleared.description: The products (`productKey`) and credit packs (`packKey`) whose open sessions were cleared.

stillProcessing.description: Present when a credit pack's payment is still processing. Those sessions are kept (and still block account deletion) until the payment lands; they never stop the rest from being cleared.

redirectUrl.description: Relative path (must start with a single `/`) to return to after checkout.

url.description: Dodo Payments hosted checkout URL for the one-time credit pack purchase.

CodedErrorResponse.description:
An error whose `details` says why in machine form. `details.code` is stable; clients branch on
it, not on the message. The other `details` fields depend on the code.

PlanChangePreviewRequest.description: An `idempotencyKey` field is accepted here too, and ignored; a preview changes nothing.

productKey.description: The plan to price. Only an upgrade to `bundle` is accepted today.

interval.description: Must match the current subscription's billing period.

productKey.description: The plan to move to. Only an upgrade to `bundle` is accepted today.

interval.description: Must match the current subscription's billing period.

idempotencyKey.description: Body alternative to the `Idempotency-Key` header; the header wins when both are sent.

dueNow.description: The total charged now for the rest of the current period (the provider's prorated quote), in the currency's minor unit.

nextAmount.description: The new plan's recurring amount before tax, in the minor unit.

status.description: The provider charges the difference; the plan moves once that payment succeeds and its webhook arrives. `GET /billing/me` shows the new plan then.

confirmed.description: False when the provider's answer never arrived (the response is then `202`); the change may still apply.

replayed.description: Always present. `true` when this is the stored answer for an idempotency key already used, `false` on a fresh call.

event.description:
Normalized to lower case with spaces as `_`. Public callers may send only `resume_created`,
`resume_deleted`, `resume_exported`, `cover_letter_exported`, `auth_otp_sent`,
`dashboard_opened`, `roadmap_viewed`, `share_link_created`, `share_link_updated` and
`share_link_revoked`. Internal callers (`x-internal-key`) may send any other name too:
one that is not a known event is stored as `custom_<name>` (a name that already starts with
`custom_` is kept as is).

value.description: Internal callers only; a public call always counts as 1.

confirmAffiliateForfeit.description: Send `true` after the user saw the `409 AFFILIATE_BALANCE_FORFEIT` amount and still wants the account deleted. The query parameter `confirmAffiliateForfeit=true` works the same way.

confirmedAffiliateForfeitCents.description: The amount the user was shown, from `details.amountCents`. If the unpaid balance has grown past it, the request is refused again with the new amount.

token.description: Same value as `slug` — the public path segment for this link.

publicPath.description:
Convenience path built from the owner's username and the link slug. Only returned by
`POST /shares`, not by the list endpoint.

hasPassword.description: The scrypt password hash itself is never returned in any API response.

allowDownload.description:
Whether the studio shows a Download button on the public page. A display preference, not a
security control: the studio hides the Download button, and viewers can still save the page.

snapshot.description: Static content snapshot captured at share time.

password.description: When provided, the link is scrypt-hashed and requires this password to view.

expiresAt.description: 7, 14, 30 or 90 days from now (within a day), or the link's current expiry to keep it. Omitted or null (without noExpiry), a new link lasts 7 days and an existing one keeps its expiry; null does not mean never. Send noExpiry true for a link that never expires.

noExpiry.description: true for a link that never expires. Not allowed together with expiresAt.

updateSlug.description: Regenerate the public slug instead of reusing the existing one (if a link already exists for this document).

allowDownload.description:
Whether the studio shows a Download button on the public page. A display preference, not a
security control: the studio hides the Download button, and viewers can still save the page.
A new link defaults to true; replacing an existing link without this field keeps its value.

PublicSharePayload.description:
While a password is required, only `passwordRequired` (`true`) and `expiresAt` are sent.
Otherwise every field below is present except `snapshot`, which is sent once no password is
required or after successful verification.

allowDownload.description:
Whether the studio shows a Download button on the public page. A display preference, not a
security control: the studio hides the Download button, and viewers can still save the page.
Not present while a password is required.

snapshot.description: Only present once no password is required, or after successful verification.

code.description: Letters, digits and hyphens. Upper case is accepted and lower-cased before the lookup.

user.description: Null when the affiliate's account is gone.

name.description: First name and last initial ("Jane D."), or null when the account has no name.

referrals.description: Most recent 50 referrals (recency-limited preview). Use totalReferrals/conversions for exact counts.

withdrawals.description: The 25 most recent withdrawals, newest first.

payoutNote.description: Visible to the affiliate. The note the admin writes when approving, rejecting or paying the withdrawal (the payout reference, or the reason for a rejection), shown on the affiliate's payouts page as written.

clawbackCents.description: Commission paid out earlier and since reversed, which is owed back.

withdrawableCents.description: What a withdrawal may request now, `availableCents` less `clawbackCents` (never below 0).

code.description: Another affiliate's code. Letters, digits and hyphens; upper case is accepted and lower-cased. Self-referrals are rejected.

data.description:
The created withdrawal row as stored: `id`, `userId`, `amountCents`, `currency`,
`status` (`REQUESTED`), `payoutNote`, `reviewedBy`, `reviewedAt`, `paidAt`,
`createdAt` and `updatedAt`.

graduationYear.description: A 4-digit year from last year to 8 years ahead, checked on each request. Surrounding spaces are trimmed.

AmbassadorStatus.description:
Intentionally small today: this surface only covers application intake and status. There is
no points/rewards/redemption API yet — that system has not been built.

role.description: The user's account role (e.g. USER, AMBASSADOR).

name.description: The account's name, so the form can greet and prefill.

application.description: The latest application's answers, so a rejected applicant can edit and resubmit; null when there is none.

Bad Request - The request body or parameters are invalid. `details` lists every failing
field as `{ path, message }`, `path` being the dotted field path.

Bad Request - The JSON body is invalid. A body that fails validation answers "Validation
failed" with `details` listing every failing field as `{ path, message }`. A body that is not
valid JSON answers "Invalid JSON body" with no `details`.

invalidJson.summary: The body is not valid JSON

PublicUnauthorizedError.description:
Unauthorized. This route needs no signed-in user, but it is not open to anonymous callers. A
request with no API key from an origin that is not a whitelisted VeriWorkly origin answers
`401` with `details.code` `API_KEY_REQUIRED`. A malformed, unknown, revoked or expired key
answers `401` with no `details`.

Unauthorized. This route takes a signed-in session only. An API key is ignored here, so a call
made with one gets this `401` too. The body has no `details`.

InsufficientScopeError.description: Forbidden - The API key does not carry the scope this operation needs.

example.message: This API key does not have permission for this action.

PayloadTooLargeError.description:
Payload Too Large - The body is larger than this route accepts (see "Response Envelope" in the
introduction for each route's limit).

RateLimitError.description:
Too Many Requests. Two limits apply to this route, and both answer `429` with `Retry-After`
(seconds):

- the per-IP limit, counted before authentication: 100 requests per 15 minutes on most
  routes, 20 per minute on the AI routes (`/ai/*`, `/ats/analyze`, `/ats/convert-resume`,
  `/profiles/import/linkedin`), plus 1,000 per 15 minutes across all routes;
- the per-key limit, when the request carries an API key: 20 requests per 15 minutes by
  default, set per key. Every keyed response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`,
  `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The key's request limit per 15 minutes. Sent only on API key requests.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window (`0` on a `429`). Sent only on API key requests.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time, in seconds, when the window resets. Sent only on API key requests.

value.message: Too many requests. Please try again later.

AutosaveRateLimitError.description:
Too Many Requests. This route is an autosave target, so it has its own limit: 600 saves per 15
minutes per user, counted after authentication. It also counts toward the 1,000 requests per
15 minutes per IP across all routes and, with an API key, the key's own limit. Every `429`
carries `Retry-After` (seconds).

value.message: Too many requests. Please try again later.
Rate limit exceeded. You are allowed 20 requests per 15 minutes. Please try again in 840 seconds.

IpRateLimitError.description:
Too Many Requests - The per-IP limit, counted before authentication: 100 requests per 15
minutes on most routes, plus 1,000 per 15 minutes across all routes. `Retry-After` gives the
seconds to wait.

Service Unavailable - Retry shortly. The session store could not be read, so the server
cannot tell whether the caller is signed in (this is not a sign-out), or the database could
not be reached.

Service Unavailable - Retry shortly. The session store could not be read, so the server cannot
tell whether the caller is signed in (this is not a sign-out), or the database could not be
reached. Neither answer carries `details`.

`AMBASSADOR_PROGRAM_ENABLED`), which is the default in production until it is turned on. This
check runs before authentication and always sends `details.code` `PROGRAM_DISABLED`. The same
status is also sent when the database cannot be reached and, on signed-in routes, when the
